title: A flat finite-type sheaf has a free affine neighbourhood over a henselian local base
statement: Let $A$ be a henselian commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $f:X\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $x\in X$ satisfy $f(x)=\mathfrak m$, and assume that its module stalk $\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], regarded as an $A$-module through $f$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then there is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ such that $\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ is a free $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The free module is not required to have finite rank.

source.place: Tag 05MF (lemma-flat-finite-type-affine-neighbourhood-projective), specialization over a henselian local base: an elementary etale neighbourhood of the closed point has the same local ring as the base. This is the specialization used in the free-affine-neighbourhood paragraph of lemma-flat-finite-type-local-colimit-free.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ containing $x$ such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra, using the locally finite-type affine cover. Choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $A$. The surjection $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$, $t_i\mapsto b_i$, realizes $X_0$ as a closed subscheme $i:X_0\hookrightarrow P=\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. This is the affine quotient characterization of a closed immersion. Put $y=i(x)$. The map $P\to S$ is finitely presented: its algebra presentation has these $n$ generators and no relations.

source.place: Tag 05MF, first three sentences of the proof: affine reduction and embedding into affine space

proof.text: Put $\mathcal G=i_*(\mathcal F|_{X_0})$. A closed immersion is finite, so the finite-pushforward theorem makes $\mathcal G$ quasi-coherent of finite type. The closed-pushforward stalk comparison gives $\mathcal G_y\cong\mathcal F_x$ compatibly with the $A$-action. Consequently $\mathcal G_y$ is flat over $A=\mathcal O_{S,\mathfrak m}$. It suffices to find an affine open $H\subseteq P$ containing $y$ with $\Gamma(H,\mathcal G)$ free over $A$: the last step will pull $H$ back along the closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 05MF, reduction from the sheaf on X to its closed pushforward on affine space

proof.text: Apply the finite-type flat-at-a-point theorem to $P\to S$, $\mathcal G$, and $y$. Its hypotheses hold: $P/S$ is locally finitely presented by step 1, $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent finite type by step 2, and its stalk at $y$ is $A$-flat. It gives an elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(S,\mathfrak m)$ and an open $V\subseteq P\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}$ containing the point above $y$, on which the pulled-back module is finitely presented and flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Replace $T$ by an affine open containing $t$; this does not change its local ring or residue field.

Here is the henselian specialization, also used in step 7. For any affine elementary etale $(T,t)\to(S,\mathfrak m)$, write $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and let $\mathfrak q$ represent $t$. The henselian etale retraction theorem gives $\sigma:D\to A$ with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$. Its section $j:S\to T$ is open and closed by the etale-section lemma. The needed separatedness holds directly: the diagonal of this affine-to-affine map is induced by the surjection $D\otimes_A D\to D$, $d\otimes d^{\prime}\mapsto dd^{\prime}$, hence is a closed immersion. Since $j(\mathfrak m)=t$, the section identifies $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $\mathcal O_{S,\mathfrak m}=A$ as an $A$-algebra. Thus the structural map $A\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is an isomorphism. For the neighbourhood of step 3 this identifies $P\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $P$ and $V$ with an open neighbourhood of $y$, with exactly the original sheaf $\mathcal G|_V$.

source.place: Tag 05U7, free-affine-neighbourhood paragraph, with Algebra Tag 04GG and Etale Morphisms Tag 024T for the henselian specialization

proof.text: Choose a basic affine open $Z=D(h)\subseteq P$ containing $y$ and contained in $V$. The restricted sheaf $\mathcal G|_Z$ is still quasi-coherent, finitely presented and flat over $A$, since these are local conditions or conditions on stalks. Moreover $Z\to S$ is finitely presented: its coordinate algebra has the explicit finite presentation $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n,u]/(hu-1)$. Apply the projective-neighbourhood theorem to $Z/S$, $\mathcal G|_Z$, and $y$. It gives an affine elementary etale $(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})\to(S,\mathfrak m)$, with $S^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}D^{\prime}$, and an affine open $W\subseteq Z\times_S S^{\prime}$ containing $(y,s^{\prime})$, with $Q=\Gamma(W,\operatorname{pr}_Z^*(\mathcal G|_Z))$ projective over $D^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 05MF, application of Tag 05ME after finite-presentation reduction; Tag 05ME statement

proof.text: Use the section $j:S\to S^{\prime}$ through $s^{\prime}$ supplied by the construction in step 4, and its ring retraction $\sigma:D^{\prime}\to A$. Base change $W$ along $j$. The scheme $H=W\times_{S^{\prime}}S$ is affine (both $W$ and the base schemes are affine), and under $(Z\times_S S^{\prime})\times_{S^{\prime}}S\cong Z$ it is an open neighbourhood of $y$. The open is obtained by inverse image of the open $W$, not merely from a set-theoretic factorization. The fibre over $(y,s^{\prime})$ is unchanged because $j(\mathfrak m)=s^{\prime}$ and the residue-field map is the specified isomorphism. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence, so the pulled-back sheaf on $W$ meets the quasi-coherence hypothesis. Affine pushforward base change for $W\to S^{\prime}$ identifies $\Gamma(H,\mathcal G|_H)$ with $A\otimes_{D^{\prime},\sigma}Q$. Pullback composition identifies the sheaf here with $\mathcal G|_H$, since the composite $H\to W\to Z$ is the open inclusion.

source.place: Tag 05U7, free-affine-neighbourhood paragraph; affine scalar change as in Coherent Tag 02KG

proof.text: Projectivity survives this scalar extension without any flatness assumption on $\sigma$: choose split maps $Q\to\bigoplus_{b\in B}D^{\prime}\to Q$ with composite $1_Q$. Tensoring these maps with $A$ gives split maps $A\otimes_{D^{\prime}}Q\to\bigoplus_{b\in B}A\to A\otimes_{D^{\prime}}Q$ with composite the identity. The direct-sum identification sends $a\otimes(d_b)_b$ to $(a\sigma(d_b))_b$ and has inverse given on the $b$-th basis vector by $a\mapsto a\otimes e_b$. Thus $\Gamma(H,\mathcal G|_H)$ is projective over $A$.

source.place: Tag 05MF, projective conclusion and arbitrary scalar extension along the henselian section; projectivity via the direct-summand characterization

proof.text: Since $A$ is local, the arbitrary-rank projective-freeness theorem makes $\Gamma(H,\mathcal G)$ free over $A$. Set $U=i^{-1}(H)\subseteq X_0\subseteq X$. This is open and contains $x$. It is affine by the affine quotient description of a closed immersion: $U$ is the closed subscheme of the affine scheme $H$ cut out by the restricted defining ideal. By the definition of direct image, $\Gamma(H,\mathcal G)=\Gamma(i^{-1}H,\mathcal F)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ as $A$-modules. Transport the free basis along this equality. This proves precisely the stated conclusion, allowing the empty basis and arbitrary infinite rank.

source.place: Tag 05MF, final application of Algebra Tag 0593 (theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring), followed by restriction back to X

Step 8 is Kaplansky 0593 and U=i^{-1}(H), which is affine. The new node lem-sfb-finitely-presented-flat-point-projective-etale-neighbourhood is exactly 05ME, hypothesis by hypothesis.
